SS_LAT_LONG_SWAP.label: Mixes up latitude and longitude
SS_LAT_LONG_SWAP.explanation: Reads a latitude as a distance east–west (or the other way round).

lat_long_meaning.title: What latitude and longitude tell you
lat_long_meaning.big_idea: A position has two parts. Latitude says how far north or south of the Equator a place is. Longitude says how far east or west of the Prime Meridian it is. Mixing them up puts you on the wrong side of the world.
steps: The number with N or S is the latitude.
The number with E or W is the longitude.
Latitude lines (parallels) run east–west; longitude lines (meridians) run north–south from pole to pole.
lat_long_meaning.sense_check: India is north of the Equator and east of the Prime Meridian, so Indian places have °N and °E.

worked_examples.prompt: Delhi is at about 29°N, 77°E. What does 29°N tell you?
worked_examples.answer: How far north or south of the Equator it is
steps: 29°N has the letter N, so it is a latitude.
It says Delhi is 29° north of the Equator.

hemispheres.title: Which hemispheres a place is in
hemispheres.big_idea: The Equator splits the Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres; the Prime Meridian splits it into Eastern and Western. The letters in a place's coordinates tell you which halves it is in.
steps: Find the latitude letter: N → Northern, S → Southern.
Find the longitude letter: E → Eastern, W → Western.
Don't assume north and east just because India is: always read the letters.
hemispheres.sense_check: Sydney is at about 34°S, 151°E: south of the Equator but east of the Prime Meridian.
